description: Merged, reviewed, source-backed Daily Knowledge corpus for BISCAAS / EM Bot. Wikipedia is excluded. Blender material is sourced from the official Blender Manual.

review.source_policy: Blender additions were restricted to docs.blender.org or Blender.org documentation hosts. Existing corpus policy remains in force.
review.verification_note: Current Blender Manual pages were confirmed through current web search results; direct page fetching from docs.blender.org returned HTTP 402 in this environment, so individual direct-page fetches could not all be independently rechecked here. The submitted Blender corpus itself identifies the official Blender 5.2 LTS Manual as its source.
review.blender_duplicate_note: Incoming Blender items with duplicate IDs, identical facts, or highly similar same-topic title/fact pairs were omitted.

items.title: Original Pong Prototype
items.fact: The Computer History Museum holds the original Pong prototype made by Allan Alcorn for Nolan Bushnell at Atari.
items.explanation: The prototype is part of the museum's game-history collection.

items.title: Pong Bar Installation
items.fact: The Pong prototype was placed in Andy Capps' bar in Sunnyvale in 1972.
items.explanation: The location was used to test the game with real players.

items.title: Computer Space and Spacewar
items.fact: Atari's Computer Space was based on Spacewar! in its concept of space combat.
items.explanation: Earlier computer games influenced the design of later arcade machines.

items.title: Atari 2600 Programming
items.fact: The Atari 2600 was known for having primitive video hardware that was challenging to program.
items.explanation: Developers had to work closely with constrained hardware capabilities.

items.title: Pitfall
items.fact: The Computer History Museum cites Pitfall! as one of the genre-defining games produced for the Atari VCS.
items.explanation: The game is presented as an example of software that pushed the platform.

items.title: Adventure
items.fact: The Computer History Museum cites Adventure as another genre-defining Atari VCS game.
items.explanation: The title is part of the historical software legacy of the console.

items.title: Unreal Actor
items.fact: An Actor is an object that can be placed into an Unreal level.
items.explanation: Cameras, static meshes, and player start locations are examples of Actors.

items.title: Actor Transform
items.fact: Actors support translation, rotation, and scale.
items.explanation: These transforms describe an Actor's position and orientation in 3D space.

items.title: Spawn Actor
items.fact: Unreal Actors can be created during gameplay by spawning them.
items.explanation: Spawning creates an instance of an Actor class at runtime.

items.title: Destroy Actor
items.fact: Unreal Actors can be destroyed through gameplay code.
items.explanation: Gameplay can remove an Actor instance from the active world.

items.title: AActor Base Class
items.fact: AActor is the base C++ class for Unreal Actors.
items.explanation: Custom C++ Actor classes derive from this engine base class.

items.title: Root Component Transform
items.fact: When an Actor has a root component, its Transform data comes from that root component.
items.explanation: The root component represents the Actor's world transform in this model.

items.title: Actor as Component Container
items.fact: Unreal documentation describes Actors as containers that hold Components.
items.explanation: Components provide the pieces of functionality that make up an Actor.

items.title: Actors
items.fact: An Actor is any object that can be placed into a level in Unreal Engine.
items.explanation: Whether it is a static mesh like a rock, a light source, or a character, if it exists in the 3D space of an Unreal Engine level, it is categorized fundamentally as an Actor.

items.title: Animation Sequence Keyframes
items.fact: Unreal Animation Sequences contain keyframes specifying skeleton position, rotation, and scale at points in time.
items.explanation: The keyframes define the poses used during sequential playback.

items.title: Animation Interpolation
items.fact: Unreal blends between sequential animation keyframes during playback.
items.explanation: The interpolation produces continuous motion from discrete keyed poses.

items.title: Shared Skeleton Animation
items.fact: Animation Sequences are tied to Skeleton assets, allowing animations to be shared by compatible meshes using the same skeleton.
items.explanation: A common skeleton provides the structural basis for reusing animation data.

items.title: State Machine
items.fact: An Animation Blueprint can contain State Machines that define which animations play and when transitions occur.
items.explanation: States represent animation situations and transitions define movement between them.

items.title: Movement State Example
items.fact: Unreal documents using animation states for situations such as idle, walking, running, and jumping.
items.explanation: A character's locomotion can be represented as separate animation states.

items.title: Blend Space Input
items.fact: A Blend Space can blend animations according to one or two dimensions of input.
items.explanation: The graph coordinates determine how poses are mixed.

items.title: Sequencer Realtime Editing
items.fact: Unreal's animation mode can edit level actors and components with Sequencer in real time.
items.explanation: Creators can build animation while seeing the result in the level.

items.title: Animation Curve
items.fact: An Unreal Animation Curve is a float-type value that can be added and keyframed inside an Animation Sequence.
items.explanation: The curve changes a numeric value over the course of an animation.

items.title: Material Parameter Animation
items.fact: Animation Curves can animate material parameters.
items.explanation: A character's animation can therefore drive material changes in sync with motion.

items.title: Morph Target Animation
items.fact: Animation Curves can animate Morph Targets.
items.explanation: A curve can drive facial or other shape deformation alongside skeletal motion.

items.title: Synchronized Properties
items.fact: Animation Curves can augment animations with additional animatable properties.
items.explanation: They let extra values change according to the same timing as skeletal animation.

items.title: Skeleton Editor
items.fact: The Skeleton Editor provides visual control of bone and joint hierarchy.
items.explanation: Artists can work on the skeletal structure associated with a Skeletal Mesh.

items.title: Skeletal Mesh Editor
items.fact: The Skeletal Mesh Editor is used to edit meshes and assign materials.
items.explanation: It also provides controls related to level of detail and morph targets.

items.title: Animation Sequence Editor
items.fact: The Animation Sequence Editor can edit and preview Animation Sequences.
items.explanation: It provides a dedicated environment for inspecting and changing sequence data.

items.title: Animation Blueprint Editor
items.fact: The Animation Blueprint Editor is a visual scripting environment for directing animation behavior.
items.explanation: It provides graphs for building runtime animation logic.

items.title: Physics Asset Editor
items.fact: The Physics Asset Editor lets users manipulate the Physics Asset assigned to a Skeletal Mesh.
items.explanation: The physics asset represents collision and physical bodies used with the skeleton.

items.title: Skeleton Sockets
items.fact: The Skeleton Editor can be used to create Skeleton Sockets.
items.explanation: Sockets provide named attachment points associated with the skeleton.

items.title: Pose Asset
items.fact: Unreal animation tools can create Pose Assets from a current pose or pose description.
items.explanation: A pose asset stores a pose for reuse in animation workflows.

items.title: Animation Montage
items.fact: Unreal animation tools can create AnimMontage assets using a selected skeleton.
items.explanation: Montages are an animation asset type used in the Unreal animation system.

items.title: Aim Offset
items.fact: Unreal animation tools can create Aim Offset Blend Spaces.
items.explanation: An Aim Offset is a blend-space-based animation asset used for directional aiming behaviors.

items.title: Behavior Trees
items.fact: Behavior Trees are used in Unreal Engine to create complex artificial intelligence logic by organizing tasks in a hierarchical flow.
items.explanation: A Behavior Tree reads the game state (like 'is the player visible?') and branches down different logic paths, deciding whether an AI character should patrol, attack, or take cover, forming the brain of the non-player character.

items.title: Blueprint Visual Scripting
items.fact: The Blueprint Visual Scripting system in Unreal Engine uses a node-based interface to create gameplay elements without writing traditional code.
items.explanation: Blueprints provide an intuitive, visual way to program game logic. Designers can connect graphical nodes representing functions, events, and variables to build complex behaviors, making game programming accessible to non-programmers.

items.title: Control Rig
items.fact: Control Rig is a scriptable rigging system that allows animators to build custom rigs and animate characters directly inside Unreal Engine.
items.explanation: Instead of animating a character in a separate program like Maya and importing it, Control Rig provides the tools to manipulate joints, create inverse kinematics, and author animations directly within the engine's editor.

items.title: Niagara
items.fact: Niagara is Unreal Engine's visual effects system.
items.explanation: It is used for creating dynamic effects in Unreal projects.

items.title: Niagara Emitter
items.fact: An emitter is a basic building block of a Niagara system.
items.explanation: Emitters are used to generate particles or effect elements.

items.title: Niagara Modules
items.fact: Modules are a basic building block of Niagara.
items.explanation: Modules provide operations that shape the behavior of an effect.

items.title: Niagara Event Handlers
items.fact: Niagara supports event handlers.
items.explanation: Event handlers provide a way for effect logic to respond to events.

items.title: Effect Baking to Flipbook
items.fact: Niagara can bake a system into a flipbook.
items.explanation: A flipbook represents the effect as a sequence of images.

items.title: Animation-Attached Effects
items.fact: Niagara learning material includes attaching effects to animation.
items.explanation: An effect can be coordinated with the motion of an animated object.

items.title: Lumen
items.fact: Lumen is Unreal Engine's fully dynamic global illumination and reflections system.
items.explanation: It calculates indirect lighting and reflections dynamically for supported projects.

items.title: Diffuse Interreflection
items.fact: Lumen renders diffuse interreflection with unlimited bounces.
items.explanation: Light can contribute through repeated diffuse interactions in the scene.

items.title: Indirect Specular Reflection
items.fact: Lumen renders indirect specular reflections.
items.explanation: Reflective surfaces can show indirect reflected light through the Lumen reflection system.

items.title: Color Bleeding
items.fact: Lumen can produce color bleed when indirect light reflects from colored surfaces.
items.explanation: A colored surface can contribute that color to nearby indirectly lit surfaces.

items.title: Large Environment Scale
items.fact: Lumen is designed for environments ranging from millimeters to kilometers.
items.explanation: The documented scale range spans small details and large worlds.

items.title: Lumen and Nanite
items.fact: Epic documents Lumen as integrating with Nanite.
items.explanation: The two systems can operate together in Unreal Engine 5 projects.

items.title: Lumen and World Partition
items.fact: Epic documents Lumen as integrating with World Partition.
items.explanation: Dynamic lighting can be used with Unreal's large-world partitioning architecture.

items.title: Lumen Light Types
items.fact: Lumen supports Directional, Sky, Point, Spot, and Rect light types.
items.explanation: These common light categories can contribute to supported Lumen scenes.

items.title: Lumen Static Lights
items.fact: Static lights are not supported by Lumen because their contributions are stored in lightmaps and disabled when Lumen is enabled.
items.explanation: Lumen uses its dynamic lighting path instead of those static-lightmap contributions.

items.title: Lumen Global Illumination
items.fact: Lumen is a fully dynamic global illumination and reflections system that reacts immediately to scene and lighting changes.
items.explanation: With Lumen, developers do not need to pre-calculate or bake lighting into textures. If a light source moves or a door opens, the bouncing light and shadows update in real-time to match the new physical state of the environment.

items.title: MetaSound
items.fact: MetaSound is a high-performance Unreal audio system built around a Digital Signal Processing graph.
items.explanation: Sound designers can construct and control audio through graph nodes.

items.title: Procedural Audio
items.fact: MetaSounds can generate audio synthetically at runtime.
items.explanation: Sound can be produced from graph logic instead of only playing fixed recordings.

items.title: Sample-Accurate Timing
items.fact: MetaSounds provide sample-accurate timing.
items.explanation: Audio events can be controlled with precision at the audio-sample level.

items.title: Audio Buffer Control
items.fact: MetaSounds provide control at the audio-buffer level.
items.explanation: Sound generation can respond to data at a fine temporal resolution.

items.title: Graph Reuse
items.fact: MetaSounds support graph reuse.
items.explanation: Common sound-generation structures can be reused in other MetaSound assets.

items.title: Gameplay Audio Data
items.fact: MetaSounds are designed to integrate with game data and player interactions.
items.explanation: Gameplay values can influence procedural sound behavior.

items.title: Nanite
items.fact: Nanite is Unreal Engine's virtualized geometry system.
items.explanation: It uses an internal mesh format and rendering technology for high-detail geometry.

items.title: Pixel-Scale Geometry
items.fact: Nanite is designed to render pixel-scale geometric detail.
items.explanation: The system can handle very fine geometry that is visible in the final image.

items.title: Visible Detail Work
items.fact: Nanite intelligently performs work on the detail that is visible on screen.
items.explanation: The renderer can avoid spending equal effort on geometry that cannot contribute visible detail.

items.title: Compressed Geometry
items.fact: Nanite's data format is highly compressed.
items.explanation: Compression helps organize large amounts of geometry data.

items.title: Fine-Grained Streaming
items.fact: Nanite supports fine-grained streaming.
items.explanation: The system can stream geometry detail in smaller portions as needed.

items.title: Automatic LOD
items.fact: Nanite supports automatic level of detail.
items.explanation: The system can select an appropriate geometric representation as viewing conditions change.

items.title: ZBrush Source Art
items.fact: Epic documents importing film-quality source art such as ZBrush sculpts for Nanite workflows.
items.explanation: High-density sculpted geometry can be used as a source for a Nanite asset.

items.title: Photogrammetry Source Art
items.fact: Epic documents photogrammetry scans as another type of film-quality source art usable with Nanite.
items.explanation: Scanned real-world geometry can serve as high-detail source content.

items.title: High-Poly Detailing
items.fact: Epic documents using high-poly detailing rather than baking all detail into normal maps with Nanite.
items.explanation: Geometry itself can carry fine shape information.

items.title: Nanite UVs
items.fact: Nanite supports multiple UV sets.
items.explanation: An asset can therefore contain more than one UV channel when its material workflow requires it.

items.title: Nanite Vertex Colors
items.fact: Nanite supports vertex colors.
items.explanation: Per-vertex color data can remain part of the Nanite mesh representation.

items.title: Nanite Materials
items.fact: Materials can be assigned to sections of Nanite meshes.
items.explanation: Different sections can use material assignments and related shading behavior.

items.title: Nanite Virtualized Geometry
items.fact: Nanite is Unreal Engine's virtualized geometry system, which uses an internal mesh format to render pixel-scale detail and high object counts.
items.explanation: Nanite allows developers to import high-quality source art consisting of millions of polygons directly into the engine. It intelligently renders only the detail that can be seen by the camera, maintaining high performance alongside cinematic visual fidelity.

items.title: Niagara VFX System
items.fact: Niagara is Unreal Engine’s primary visual effects system, utilizing a node-based interface to program particle behaviors.
items.explanation: Artists use Niagara to create complex effects like fire, smoke, magic spells, and rain. Its modular design allows data to be shared and reused across multiple different particle emitters.

items.title: Blueprints
items.fact: Unreal Blueprints are a visual scripting language with a node-based interface.
items.explanation: Developers can create gameplay logic by connecting visual nodes.

items.title: Typed Blueprint Data
items.fact: Blueprints work with typed data such as numbers, booleans, arrays, and structs.
items.explanation: Variables and pins have defined data types.

items.title: Execution Wires
items.fact: Blueprint logic flows through execution wires.
items.explanation: A node runs when execution reaches it through the graph.

items.title: Blueprint Class
items.fact: A Blueprint Class is an asset for adding functionality on top of an existing gameplay class.
items.explanation: It defines a reusable type that can be placed into a level.

items.title: Blueprint Reuse
items.fact: Instances of a Blueprint Class can be placed into levels.
items.explanation: One Blueprint definition can therefore be used to create multiple world objects.

items.title: Blueprint Components
items.fact: Blueprints can contain components such as collision, static mesh, skeletal mesh, and movement components.
items.explanation: A Blueprint can assemble an Actor from reusable pieces.

items.title: Blueprint Event Graph
items.fact: A Level Blueprint contains a level-wide global event graph.
items.explanation: It can provide level-specific logic and bind events to Actors in the level.

items.title: Data-Only Blueprint
items.fact: A Blueprint Class can contain only inherited variables or components without execution logic.
items.explanation: Such a Blueprint can act as a configured reusable object without a custom script graph.

items.title: C++ and Blueprint Bridge
items.fact: Unreal C++ includes Blueprint-specific markup that lets programmers expose systems for designers to extend.
items.explanation: C++ and visual scripting can therefore be combined in one project.

items.title: Pawns
items.fact: A Pawn is a subclass of Actor that can be controlled by players or AI.
items.explanation: While all Pawns are Actors, not all Actors are Pawns. Pawns contain the specific logic required to receive input commands, allowing them to serve as the physical representation of a player or a non-player character within the game world.

items.title: PlayerController
items.fact: The PlayerController acts as the interface between the human player and the Pawn they are controlling in the game world.
items.explanation: It translates physical inputs from a keyboard or gamepad into game actions. It is fundamentally an invisible entity that 'possesses' a physical character, allowing input rules to persist even if the character dies or changes.

items.title: Skeletal Mesh
items.fact: An Unreal Skeletal Mesh asset contains a character's visual mesh and skeleton bone data.
items.explanation: The asset combines the deformable geometry with the structure used to animate it.

items.title: Skeleton Asset
items.fact: An imported character's skeleton becomes a separate Skeleton asset in Unreal.
items.explanation: The skeleton asset can be viewed and edited in the Skeleton Editor.

items.title: Animation Sequence Asset
items.fact: FBX animations imported with a character can become Animation Sequence assets.
items.explanation: The sequences store animation data that can be played on a compatible skeletal mesh.

items.title: Animation Sequence Playback
items.fact: Animation Sequences can be dynamically played using Character and Animation Blueprints.
items.explanation: Blueprint logic can choose and control animation playback at runtime.

items.title: Sequencer Animation
items.fact: Animation Sequences can also be used in authored cinematics through Sequencer.
items.explanation: The same animation asset can contribute to a cinematic sequence.

items.title: Character Blueprint
items.fact: Unreal documentation uses a Character Blueprint to combine a Skeletal Mesh with game and animation logic.
items.explanation: The Blueprint organizes the mesh and behaviors of a playable character.

items.title: Animation Blueprint
items.fact: An Animation Blueprint can contain an Anim Graph that selects Animation Sequences based on Blueprint logic.
items.explanation: It can choose the appropriate animation according to gameplay variables.

items.title: Blend Spaces
items.fact: Animation Blueprints can use Blend Spaces to blend animation based on inputs or variables.
items.explanation: A Blend Space maps values to animation poses or sequences for smooth transitions.

items.title: Mesh Deformers
items.fact: Unreal deformer techniques can transform mesh geometry instead of bones.
items.explanation: Deformers can be used for detailed effects such as facial, clothing, or muscle movement.

items.title: Modular Characters
items.fact: Unreal documents modular characters built from multiple skeletal meshes.
items.explanation: Separate mesh pieces can be assembled to create changing outfits or character variants.

sources.title: Unreal Engine Documentation, Epic Developer Community

items.title: Nanite with Landscape Terrain
items.fact: Unreal Engine allows Nanite to be applied to Landscape terrain, which can improve rendering performance, particularly in combination with Virtual Shadow Maps.
items.explanation: Because the underlying source data doesn't change, end users see no visual difference when a Landscape switches to using Nanite; the benefit is purely one of performance.

source.name: Unreal Engine Documentation, Epic Developer Community

items.title: World Partition
items.fact: World Partition is an automatic data management and distance-based level streaming system that removes the need to manually divide large worlds into sub-levels.
items.explanation: For open-world games, loading the entire map at once would crash a computer. World Partition stores the world in a grid and dynamically loads only the cells immediately surrounding the player, seamlessly managing memory in the background.

items.title: Unreal Engine Audio File Formats
items.fact: Unreal Engine supports importing uncompressed little endian 16-bit WAV files at any sample rate.
items.explanation: WAV is a standard uncompressed audio format that provides high quality for game sound effects and music. Unreal Engine recommends sample rates of 44100 Hz or 22050 Hz, and its audio system provides tools to shape sounds and give them the desired feel in the game.

items.title: Component
items.fact: An Unreal Component is a special type of Object that an Actor can attach as a sub-object.
items.explanation: Components add reusable functionality to Actors.

items.title: Actor Component
items.fact: UActorComponent is the base class for Unreal Components.
items.explanation: It is the common base for components used to add behavior to Actors.

items.title: Actor Component Behavior
items.fact: Actor Components are suited to abstract behaviors such as movement, inventory, and attribute management.
items.explanation: They handle functionality that does not require a physical location.

items.title: Scene Component
items.fact: USceneComponent adds location-based behavior to an Actor Component.
items.explanation: A Scene Component has a transform and therefore has a place in the world.

items.title: Primitive Component
items.fact: UPrimitiveComponent is a Scene Component with a geometric representation.
items.explanation: Primitive Components can represent renderable or collidable geometry.

items.title: Collision Primitive
items.fact: Box, capsule, and sphere components can provide invisible collision geometry.
items.explanation: These shapes can be used to represent collision boundaries without rendering a visible model.

items.title: Static Mesh Component
items.fact: A Static Mesh Component contains pre-built geometry that can be rendered.
items.explanation: It is used for geometry that does not use skeletal deformation.

items.title: Skeletal Mesh Component
items.fact: A Skeletal Mesh Component contains pre-built geometry for a skeletal mesh.
items.explanation: It can represent characters and other deformable animated meshes.

items.title: Audio Component
items.fact: An Unreal Audio Component can give an Actor the ability to play sounds.
items.explanation: Attaching the component makes audio part of the Actor's assembled functionality.

items.title: Movement Component
items.fact: Movement Components can provide movement controls as part of a Blueprint or Actor.
items.explanation: A movement component packages movement behavior into a reusable component.

items.title: Component Registration
items.fact: Components need to be registered for the engine to update them and let them affect the scene.
items.explanation: Registration puts the component into the engine's active systems.

items.title: Blueprint Visual Scripting in Unreal
items.fact: Blueprint visual scripting in Unreal Engine is a complete gameplay scripting system based on a node-based interface.
items.explanation: Blueprints allow developers to create gameplay functionality without writing traditional code. Using a visual node-based interface, designers and artists can implement complex game logic, define object behaviors, and create interactive systems entirely within the Unreal Editor.

items.title: Blueprint Class in Unreal
items.fact: A Blueprint Class defines new classes or Actor types that can be instantiated and placed in maps.
items.explanation: Blueprint Classes are ideal for creating interactive objects like doors, switches, collectible items, and destructible scenery. Editing a Blueprint Class updates all its instances throughout the project, making it efficient for managing reusable game elements.

items.title: Level Blueprint in Unreal
items.fact: Every Unreal Engine level has a Level Blueprint that contains logic specific to that level's events.
items.explanation: The Level Blueprint can reference and manipulate Actors in the level, control cinematics using Level Sequence Actors, and manage level streaming. It also interacts with Blueprint Classes placed in the level.

sources.title: Unreal Engine Documentation, Epic Developer Community

items.title: Nanite Vertex Quantization
items.fact: Nanite reduces the memory and disk footprint of meshes by quantizing vertex positions, using a Position Precision setting that can be tuned per mesh.
items.explanation: Quantization means storing position values with a limited, power-of-two step size instead of full precision, which trades a small amount of accuracy for major storage savings.

items.title: Nanite Virtualized Geometry
items.fact: Nanite is Unreal Engine's virtualized geometry system, which uses an internal mesh format and rendering approach designed to display pixel-scale detail and very high object counts.
items.explanation: Instead of processing an entire high-detail mesh every frame, Nanite focuses rendering work only on the detail that can actually be seen on screen.

source.name: Unreal Engine Documentation, Epic Developer Community

items.title: Unreal Engine Fundamentals
items.fact: New Unreal Engine users should become familiar with the Unreal Editor interface, Blueprint visual scripting, and the types of content used inside an Unreal project.
items.explanation: The Unreal Editor is the primary workspace for building games. Blueprint visual scripting allows creators to build gameplay logic without writing code, and understanding content types helps organize art, audio, and other assets efficiently.

items.title: Levels in Unreal Engine
items.fact: Levels in Unreal Engine contain everything a player can see and interact with, including environments, usable objects, and other characters.
items.explanation: Levels, sometimes called Maps, are the building blocks of game worlds. Every Unreal Engine project contains at least one Level, and developers can create multiple Levels to represent different areas, chapters, or gameplay spaces.

items.title: Actors in Unreal Engine
items.fact: Unreal projects contain Actors, which are individual pieces of content that can have one or more Components attached to them.
items.explanation: Actors are the foundational objects that can be placed in Levels. Every object that exists in a game world, from static scenery to interactive characters, is an Actor. Components add specific behaviors and properties to Actors.

items.title: Assets in Unreal Engine
items.fact: Any piece of content in an Unreal Engine project is called an Asset.
items.explanation: Assets include all the individual files and resources that make up a game, such as 3D models, textures, animations, sound files, and scripts. The Content Browser is the primary tool for creating, importing, organizing, and managing Assets.

items.title: Unreal Engine Learning Tracks
items.fact: Unreal Engine offers learning tracks for programmers, designers, and artists.
items.explanation: The Programmer Track teaches coding a first-person adventure game from scratch. The Designer Track covers building levels and puzzles using Blueprints. The Artist Track focuses on in-editor workflows and tools for performing art passes on game worlds.

items.title: Packaging in Unreal Engine
items.fact: Packaging a project in Unreal Engine creates a standalone game that can run on target platforms independently of the Unreal Editor.
items.explanation: Once development is complete, Unreal Engine can package the game into a working application for Windows, macOS, Linux, consoles, and mobile devices. This packaged game can be distributed and played without requiring the Unreal Editor to be installed.

items.title: SeExpr Expression Language
items.fact: SeExpr is an embeddable, arithmetic expression language developed by Disney Animation for flexible artistic control in computer graphics.
items.explanation: SeExpr enables procedural geometry synthesis, image synthesis, simulation control, crowd animation, and geometry deformation. It was released as open source to share this technology with the broader community.

items.title: Disney Animation's Render Farm Pipeline
items.fact: At Walt Disney Animation Studios, after a shot is fully lit, artists send it to a render farm to calculate final images with Hyperion, then track the job's progress using a tool called Coda.
items.explanation: This shows how a single animated shot moves through several specialized software tools and dedicated computing resources before it becomes a finished frame.

items.title: Disney's Hyperion Renderer
items.fact: Hyperion is Walt Disney Animation Studios' in-house renderer, and it works as a physically based path tracer.
items.explanation: A renderer takes a scene's models, textures, animation, and lighting and calculates the final image by simulating how light behaves, which is what a path tracer does.

items.title: How Path Tracing Simulates Light
items.fact: Path tracing, the technique behind Disney's Hyperion renderer, generates an image by shooting rays into a virtual scene and tracking how they bounce between objects.
items.explanation: This bounce-by-bounce simulation is what allows path-traced renders to capture realistic indirect lighting, such as light reflecting off one wall to softly illuminate another.

items.title: Orbit with MMB
items.fact: Dragging `MMB` orbits the view around the point of interest.
items.explanation: Orbiting changes viewing direction without changing the modeled geometry.

items.title: Cancel Orbit
items.fact: `RMB` cancels an orbit operation.
items.explanation: The canceled operation leaves the prior view orientation unchanged.

items.title: Orbit Point of Interest
items.fact: `Alt`-`MMB` on a point makes that point the center of orbit.
items.explanation: This helps center navigation around a particular model feature.

items.title: Axis Snapped Orbit
items.fact: Holding `Alt` while orbiting can align the view to a world axis and make it orthographic.
items.explanation: Axis alignment provides a precise inspection orientation.

items.title: Discrete Vertical Orbit
items.fact: `Numpad8` and `Numpad2` orbit up and down in steps.
items.explanation: Discrete orbiting is useful when a consistent viewpoint is needed.

items.title: Discrete Horizontal Orbit
items.fact: `Numpad4` and `Numpad6` orbit left and right in steps.
items.explanation: These commands change the view direction in fixed increments.

items.title: Opposite View
items.fact: `Numpad9` switches to the opposite side of the current view.
items.explanation: The view rotates 180 degrees around the Z axis.

items.title: Roll View
items.fact: `Shift`-`Numpad4` and `Shift`-`Numpad6` roll the viewport camera.
items.explanation: Roll rotates the view around its viewing direction.

items.title: Pan
items.fact: `Shift`-`MMB` pans the view.
items.explanation: Panning moves the view without rotating its orientation.

items.title: Zoom
items.fact: The mouse wheel or `Ctrl`-`MMB` changes the viewport zoom.
items.explanation: Zoom moves the view closer to or farther from the point of interest.

items.title: Discrete Zoom
items.fact: `NumpadPlus` and `NumpadMinus` zoom in fixed steps.
items.explanation: These shortcuts provide repeatable zoom increments.

items.title: Zoom Region
items.fact: `Shift`-`B` activates Zoom Region.
items.explanation: Dragging a rectangle zooms the view to the chosen region.

items.title: Dolly
items.fact: `Shift`-`Ctrl`-`MMB` performs a dolly movement.
items.explanation: Dolly moves the view toward or away from the point of interest rather than just changing zoom.

items.title: Dolly Perspective
items.fact: Dolly changes an orthographic view to perspective.
items.explanation: Orthographic projection does not respond to forward/backward motion like a perspective view.

items.title: Frame All
items.fact: `Home` frames all objects.
items.explanation: The view is adjusted so the scene contents fit within the viewport.

items.title: Frame Selected
items.fact: `NumpadPeriod` frames the selected object or objects.
items.explanation: It centers and fits the current selection in view.

items.title: Frame Last Stroke
items.fact: `NumpadPeriod` also frames the last brush stroke in paint and sculpt modes.
items.explanation: This is useful when working on a small portion of a large mesh.

items.title: Polygon Reduction
items.fact: The Decimate modifier reduces the vertex and face count of a mesh while attempting to preserve its shape.
items.explanation: It is useful when a detailed mesh needs fewer polygons.

items.title: Decimate for Sculpt Results
items.fact: Blender documents Decimate as useful for reducing complex meshes produced by sculpting or applied subdivision.
items.explanation: It can reduce geometry after a detail-heavy workflow.

items.title: Performance Increase
items.fact: Reducing polygon count with Decimate can provide a performance increase.
items.explanation: Fewer faces generally mean less geometric data to process.

items.title: Collapse Mode
items.fact: Collapse mode progressively merges vertices while considering the shape of the mesh.
items.explanation: It reduces geometry by collapsing parts of the mesh.

items.title: Decimate Ratio
items.fact: The Ratio controls the proportion of faces to keep after decimation.
items.explanation: A lower ratio requests a smaller resulting face count.

items.title: No Edit Mode Preview
items.fact: Unlike most Blender modifiers, Decimate does not allow the changes to be visualized in Edit Mode.
items.explanation: The decimated result is primarily evaluated through the modifier result rather than an editable preview.

items.title: Array Modifier
items.fact: Array is a built-in Generate modifier.
items.explanation: It is part of Blender’s collection of geometry-generating modifiers.

items.title: Bevel Modifier
items.fact: Bevel is a built-in Generate modifier.
items.explanation: It creates beveled geometry procedurally from object geometry.

items.title: Boolean Modifier
items.fact: Boolean is a built-in Generate modifier.
items.explanation: It provides procedural Boolean geometry operations.

items.title: Build Modifier
items.fact: Build is a built-in Generate modifier.
items.explanation: It can progressively reveal generated geometry.

items.title: Curve to Tube Modifier
items.fact: Curve to Tube is a built-in Generate modifier.
items.explanation: It generates tube-like geometry from curve data.

items.title: Decimate Modifier
items.fact: Decimate is a built-in Generate modifier.
items.explanation: It is used to reduce mesh complexity.

items.title: Edge Split Modifier
items.fact: Edge Split is a built-in Generate modifier.
items.explanation: It changes how mesh edges are represented for shading and geometry.

items.title: Mask Modifier
items.fact: Mask is a built-in Generate modifier.
items.explanation: It uses vertex-group-based control to mask geometry in the modifier stack.

items.title: Mesh to Volume Modifier
items.fact: Mesh to Volume is a built-in Generate modifier.
items.explanation: It converts mesh geometry into volume data.

items.title: Mirror Modifier
items.fact: Mirror is a built-in Generate modifier.
items.explanation: It procedurally mirrors geometry across chosen axes.

items.title: Multiresolution Modifier
items.fact: Multiresolution is a built-in Generate modifier.
items.explanation: It provides multiple mesh subdivision levels used by sculpting and other workflows.

items.title: Remesh Modifier
items.fact: Remesh is a built-in Generate modifier.
items.explanation: It rebuilds mesh topology into a remeshed result.

items.title: Screw Modifier
items.fact: Screw is a built-in Generate modifier.
items.explanation: It creates geometry through a rotational extrusion workflow.

items.title: Skin Modifier
items.fact: Skin is a built-in Generate modifier.
items.explanation: It can generate a surface around a skeletal edge structure.

items.title: Solidify Modifier
items.fact: Solidify is a built-in Generate modifier.
items.explanation: It can add thickness to surface geometry.

items.title: Subdivision Surface Modifier
items.fact: Subdivision Surface is a built-in Generate modifier.
items.explanation: It generates smoother, denser geometry from the base mesh.

items.title: Triangulate Modifier
items.fact: Triangulate is a built-in Generate modifier.
items.explanation: It converts polygonal faces into triangles.

items.title: Volume to Mesh Modifier
items.fact: Volume to Mesh is a built-in Generate modifier.
items.explanation: It generates a mesh from volume data.

items.title: Weld Modifier
items.fact: Weld is a built-in Generate modifier.
items.explanation: It merges nearby vertices according to the modifier’s settings.

items.title: Wireframe Modifier
items.fact: Wireframe is a built-in Generate modifier.
items.explanation: It turns mesh edges into a wireframe-like surface representation.

items.title: Material Preview
items.fact: The Material Preview panel provides a quick visualization of the active material in a simple scene.
items.explanation: It is useful for inspecting material appearance without constructing a full final scene.

items.title: Preview Plane
items.fact: Material Preview can show a material on a plane.
items.explanation: The plane provides a simple reference surface.

items.title: Preview Sphere
items.fact: Material Preview can show a material on a sphere.
items.explanation: A sphere reveals how material shading responds across curved surfaces.

items.title: Preview Cube
items.fact: Material Preview can show a material on a cube.
items.explanation: A cube provides simple planar and edge responses for inspection.

items.title: Preview Hair
items.fact: Material Preview can preview materials on a hair shape.
items.explanation: This provides a specialized reference for hair-like shading.

items.title: Preview Shader Ball
items.fact: Material Preview includes a shader-ball shape.
items.explanation: Shader balls are useful for evaluating complex surface response.

items.title: Preview Cloth
items.fact: Material Preview includes a cloth shape.
items.explanation: The cloth shape provides a surface reference with folds.

items.title: Preview Fluid
items.fact: Material Preview includes a fluid shape.
items.explanation: This gives a material a specialized preview context.

items.title: Preview World Cycles Only
items.fact: The material-preview option to use the current scene world is documented for Cycles.
items.explanation: It uses the scene environment for preview lighting in that context.

items.title: Stencil Mapping
items.fact: Stencil mapping projects a texture from camera space onto the mesh or canvas.
items.explanation: It is designed for stamping textures for projection painting.

items.title: Stencil Boundary
items.fact: Painting with a stencil affects only the area inside the stencil boundaries.
items.explanation: The stencil therefore acts as a projected mask for texture application.

items.title: Stencil Move Shortcut
items.fact: With a stencil texture, `RMB` moves the stencil.
items.explanation: Movement repositions the projected texture in screen space.

items.title: Stencil Scale Shortcut
items.fact: With a stencil texture, `Shift`-`RMB` scales the stencil.
items.explanation: Scaling changes the size of the projected texture.

items.title: Stencil Rotate Shortcut
items.fact: With a stencil texture, `Ctrl`-`RMB` rotates the stencil.
items.explanation: Rotation changes the orientation of the projected texture.

items.title: Stencil Axis Constraint
items.fact: During stencil scaling, `X` and `Y` constrain scaling to one axis.
items.explanation: This helps control non-uniform stencil scaling.

items.title: Stencil Reset Transform
items.fact: Reset Transform restores the stencil’s position.
items.explanation: It returns the stencil to its reset location.

items.title: Inverse Kinematics (IK)
items.fact: Inverse Kinematics is an animation method where the position of an end bone determines the rotation of its parent bones.
items.explanation: Instead of rotating a character's shoulder, then the elbow, to place a hand on a table, an animator using IK simply places the hand on the table. The software automatically calculates how the arm joints should bend to reach that position.

items.title: Armature Pose
items.fact: A Blender armature can be configured into poses by transforming its bones.
items.explanation: Bone transformations deform or transform the skinned object.

items.title: Rest Position
items.fact: An armature's Edit Mode defines its default rest position.
items.explanation: The rest position is the reference configuration of the rig.

items.title: Pose Mode
items.fact: Blender provides Pose Mode specifically for configuring armature poses.
items.explanation: Pose Mode changes bones relative to their rest configuration.

items.title: Bone Transform
items.fact: Each bone has position, rotation, and scale values.
items.explanation: Those transform values determine the bone's current pose.

items.title: Pose as Offset
items.fact: A Pose Mode edit creates a transform offset from the rest position.
items.explanation: The animated pose can be understood as a change relative to the rig's base state.

items.title: Constraint Color
items.fact: Blender can display constrained bones with a green bone-state color when state colors are enabled.
items.explanation: Viewport colors can help identify constrained parts of a rig.

items.title: IK Color
items.fact: Blender can display bones with an IK Solver constraint using a yellow bone-state color when state colors are enabled.
items.explanation: The color gives a visual clue that inverse-kinematics control affects the bone.

items.title: Targetless Solver Color
items.fact: Blender can display bones with a targetless solver constraint using an orange state color when state colors are enabled.
items.explanation: Bone-state colors can reveal a specific constraint type in the viewport.

items.title: Animation and Rigging in Blender
items.fact: Blender's animation system includes keyframes, drivers, constraints, armatures, and shape keys.
items.explanation: Keyframes define poses or values at specific times; drivers allow properties to be controlled by other properties; constraints restrict or guide movement; armatures are skeleton structures for character animation; and shape keys enable facial expressions and morphing.

items.title: Shape Keys
items.fact: Shape keys in Blender are used to deform objects into new shapes for animation, and are primarily used for facial animation and muscle tweaking.
items.explanation: Instead of moving individual bones to change a character's expression, artists use shape keys to save specific mesh deformations, such as a smile or a blink. These keys can then be blended together dynamically over time.

items.title: View Layer Selection
items.fact: The Render Layers node can choose a View Layer.
items.explanation: The chosen layer determines which render information is provided.

items.title: External Scene Raw Output
items.fact: To use compositing output from another scene rather than raw render output, Blender documents rendering that scene to multilayer images such as OpenEXR and loading them with an Image node.
items.explanation: Multilayer image files preserve multiple render passes for later compositing.

items.title: Local View
items.fact: Local View isolates the selected objects so they are the only visible objects in the viewport.
items.explanation: It is useful when other scene objects obstruct the area being edited.

items.title: Local View Shortcut
items.fact: `NumpadSlash` toggles Local View.
items.explanation: Use it to quickly isolate selected objects.

items.title: Local View for Heavy Scenes
items.fact: Blender documents Local View as a way to speed up viewport performance in heavy scenes.
items.explanation: Reducing visible scene content can make interactive work easier.

items.title: Local View Is Contextual
items.fact: Local View is set per 3D Viewport.
items.explanation: Different viewports can have different local-view states.

items.title: Recover Missing Objects
items.fact: If many objects suddenly seem to vanish, pressing `NumpadSlash` can return from Local View.
items.explanation: Accidental Local View activation can look like objects were deleted when they are simply hidden from that viewport.

items.title: Remove from Local View
items.fact: `Alt`-`NumpadSlash` removes selected objects from Local View.
items.explanation: This provides more selective control over which isolated objects remain.

items.title: Compositor
items.fact: Blender's Compositor manages nodes for compositing.
items.explanation: It provides a node-based environment for processing and combining image information.

items.title: Scene Compositor Tree
items.fact: Each Blender Scene can have its own compositor node tree.
items.explanation: Different scenes can use different post-processing setups.

items.title: Reusable Compositor Node Group
items.fact: Blender can use custom compositor node groups for reuse.
items.explanation: A node setup can be packaged so the same processing structure can be reused.

items.title: Pinned Node Tree
items.fact: The Compositor can pin a node tree for display regardless of the active scene.
items.explanation: Pinning keeps the chosen tree visible while switching scenes.

items.title: Compositor Asset Shelf
items.fact: Blender's Asset Shelf can expose compositor node-group assets.
items.explanation: Reusable compositing setups can be inserted through an asset workflow.

items.title: Dope Sheet Overview
items.fact: The Dope Sheet provides a bird’s-eye view of keyframes in a scene.
items.explanation: It lets animators inspect timing across many animated properties.

items.title: Classical Animation Timing
items.fact: The Dope Sheet is inspired by classical hand-drawn animation charts showing when drawings, sounds, and camera moves occur.
items.explanation: Digital timing tools preserve the idea of a production timing chart.

items.title: Dope Sheet Modes
items.fact: The Dope Sheet has multiple modes including Dope Sheet, Action Editor, Shape Key Editor, Grease Pencil, and Mask.
items.explanation: Different modes expose different kinds of animatable data.

items.title: Action Editor
items.fact: Action Editor is a Dope Sheet mode.
items.explanation: It provides an animation-focused view for actions.

items.title: Shape Key Editor
items.fact: Shape Key Editor is a Dope Sheet mode.
items.explanation: It focuses on keyframes for shape-key animation.

items.title: Grease Pencil Dope Sheet
items.fact: Grease Pencil is a Dope Sheet mode.
items.explanation: It provides timing control for Grease Pencil animation.

items.title: Mask Dope Sheet
items.fact: Mask is a Dope Sheet mode.
items.explanation: It exposes keyframed mask-related data.

items.title: Keyframe Channels
items.fact: The Dope Sheet displays channels for animatable properties.
items.explanation: Channels organize different animated properties vertically in the editor.

items.title: Keyframe Time Axis
items.fact: Keyframes are laid out along a time axis.
items.explanation: Their horizontal location represents when the keyed value occurs.

items.title: Held Key
items.fact: A gray bar between keyframes indicates a held key when two keyframes are identical.
items.explanation: The value remains unchanged across that interval.

items.title: Custom Interpolation Indicator
items.fact: A green line segment indicates custom interpolation between keys.
items.explanation: The editor uses visual cues to communicate interpolation information.

items.title: Curve Extremes
items.fact: Up and down arrows can mark local curve maxima and minima when enabled.
items.explanation: They help identify high and low points in an animation curve.

items.title: Non-Linear Animation (NLA) Editor
items.fact: The NLA Editor allows animators to manipulate and blend separate animation actions like video clips.
items.explanation: Instead of animating a character walking and waving simultaneously from scratch, an animator can take a pre-made 'walk cycle' clip and a 'wave' clip, layer them in the NLA Editor, and have the software blend the two motions together smoothly.

items.title: Grease Pencil
items.fact: Grease Pencil is a Blender object system for drawing information in 3D space.
items.explanation: It connects drawn strokes with Blender's 3D scene.

items.title: Grease Pencil Strokes
items.fact: Grease Pencil drawings are represented using points organized as strokes.
items.explanation: The points form the visible drawn lines.

items.title: Grease Pencil 2D Animation
items.fact: Grease Pencil can be used for traditional 2D animation.
items.explanation: Artists can create drawn frame-based animation in Blender.

items.title: Grease Pencil Cut-Out
items.fact: Grease Pencil can be used for cut-out animation.
items.explanation: Drawn elements can be organized into an animation workflow based on reusable parts.

items.title: Grease Pencil Motion Graphics
items.fact: Grease Pencil can be used for motion graphics.
items.explanation: Drawings can become animated graphic elements within a 3D scene.

items.title: Grease Pencil Storyboarding
items.fact: Grease Pencil can be used as a storyboard tool.
items.explanation: Artists can sketch shots directly inside a 3D environment.

items.title: Draw Mode
items.fact: Grease Pencil strokes are created in Draw Mode.
items.explanation: Draw Mode is the creation workspace for new strokes.

items.title: Edit Mode
items.fact: Existing Grease Pencil strokes can be edited in Edit Mode.
items.explanation: Edit Mode changes already-created drawing geometry.

items.title: Sculpt Mode
items.fact: Existing Grease Pencil strokes can also be adjusted in Sculpt Mode.
items.explanation: Sculpt tools provide another way to reshape stroke data.

items.title: Grease Pencil Materials
items.fact: Grease Pencil strokes and fills can use materials.
items.explanation: Materials control how the drawn elements are displayed.

items.title: Grease Pencil Effects
items.fact: Grease Pencil supports visual effects including blur and pixelation.
items.explanation: Effects can change the appearance of a drawing without redrawing its strokes.

items.title: Grease Pencil Onion Skinning
items.fact: Grease Pencil supports onion skinning.
items.explanation: Onion skinning helps animators compare nearby frames while drawing motion.

items.title: Grease Pencil
items.fact: Grease Pencil is a specific type of Blender object that allows artists to draw 2D art directly in 3D space.
items.explanation: This tool revolutionizes traditional animation by combining 2D drawing with 3D camera movements and lighting. Artists can sketch flat, hand-drawn lines that exist on planes within a full 3D environment.

items.title: Grease Pencil Modifiers
items.fact: Grease Pencil has its own set of modifiers.
items.explanation: These operations can affect Grease Pencil objects without directly editing their base data.

items.title: Generate Modifier Category
items.fact: Grease Pencil Generate modifiers can change appearance or add geometry.
items.explanation: Generate operations are constructive changes to the evaluated drawing.

items.title: Deform Modifier Category
items.fact: Grease Pencil Deform modifiers change shape.
items.explanation: They alter the evaluated form without requiring new drawing geometry.

items.title: Color Modifier Category
items.fact: Grease Pencil Color modifiers affect color.
items.explanation: Color processing can be applied procedurally to stroke output.

items.title: Edit Modifier Category
items.fact: Grease Pencil Edit modifiers work on drawing data in editing-oriented ways.
items.explanation: They can adjust attributes such as mapping or timing without rebuilding the drawing manually.

items.title: Grease Pencil Modifier System
items.fact: Grease Pencil has its own modifier set.
items.explanation: These modifiers provide automated changes to Grease Pencil objects.

items.title: Grease Pencil Edit Modifiers
items.fact: Grease Pencil modifiers include Edit operations.
items.explanation: Edit modifiers automate changes to existing stroke data.

items.title: Grease Pencil Generate Modifiers
items.fact: Grease Pencil modifiers include Generate operations.
items.explanation: Generate modifiers can construct additional stroke geometry or appearance.

items.title: Grease Pencil Deform Modifiers
items.fact: Grease Pencil modifiers include Deform operations.
items.explanation: Deform modifiers change stroke shape without requiring manual editing.

items.title: Grease Pencil Color Modifiers
items.fact: Grease Pencil modifiers include Color operations.
items.explanation: Color modifiers change color-related output.

items.title: Grease Pencil Non-Destructive Workflow
items.fact: Grease Pencil modifiers can be combined in a stack.
items.explanation: The stack lets multiple automated operations be layered.

items.title: Apply Grease Pencil Modifier
items.fact: Applying a Grease Pencil modifier converts its evaluated result into actual stroke data and removes the modifier.
items.explanation: The generated result becomes part of the object data instead of remaining a live operation.

items.title: Blender 3D Creation Suite
items.fact: Blender is a free and open source 3D creation suite that provides tools for modeling, sculpting, texturing, rigging, animation, simulation, rendering, compositing, and video editing.
items.explanation: Blender is a complete 3D production pipeline in a single application. It is maintained by a global community and used by artists, studios, and hobbyists for creating 3D content across various industries.

items.title: Save File
items.fact: `Ctrl`-`S` saves the current Blender file.
items.explanation: Saving frequently creates recovery points for the current project file.

items.title: New File
items.fact: `Ctrl`-`N` creates a new Blender file.
items.explanation: This shortcut starts a new file using Blender’s file-creation workflow.

items.title: Open File
items.fact: `Ctrl`-`O` opens a Blender file.
items.explanation: Use it to load an existing project.

items.title: Undo
items.fact: `Ctrl`-`Z` performs Undo.
items.explanation: Undo reverses a recent operation in the current context.

items.title: Redo
items.fact: `Shift`-`Ctrl`-`Z` performs Redo.
items.explanation: Redo restores an action that was undone.

items.title: Help Search
items.fact: `F1` opens context-sensitive Help.
items.explanation: Help can be opened for the context currently under the mouse.

items.title: Rename
items.fact: `F2` renames the active item.
items.explanation: It provides a quick way to rename selected datablocks or objects.

items.title: Menu Search
items.fact: `F3` opens Menu Search.
items.explanation: Menu Search lets you find operators without navigating through menus.

items.title: Adjust Last Operation
items.fact: `F9` opens Adjust Last Operation.
items.explanation: After an operation, this panel exposes parameters that can still be adjusted.

items.title: Render Current Frame
items.fact: `F12` renders the current frame.
items.explanation: It invokes the active render process for the current frame.

items.title: Show Render
items.fact: `F11` shows the render window.
items.explanation: This provides a quick way to inspect rendered output.

items.title: Maximize Area
items.fact: `Ctrl`-`Spacebar` toggles the current area between normal and maximized display.
items.explanation: Maximizing an editor gives it more screen space.

items.title: Quick Favorites
items.fact: `Q` opens Quick Access favorites.
items.explanation: Frequently used operators can be accessed through this menu.

items.title: Delete Selected
items.fact: `X` deletes the selected item with confirmation.
items.explanation: The confirmation helps prevent accidental deletion.

items.title: Delete Without Confirmation
items.fact: `Delete` deletes the selected item without a confirmation dialog.
items.explanation: This is faster but removes the confirmation step.

items.title: Select All
items.fact: `A` selects all in editors that support the common selection shortcut.
items.explanation: Selection becomes global within the active editor context.

items.title: Deselect All
items.fact: `Alt`-`A` deselects all.
items.explanation: It clears the current selection in supported editors.

items.title: Invert Selection
items.fact: `Ctrl`-`I` inverts the selection.
items.explanation: Selected elements become unselected and unselected elements become selected.

items.title: Hide Selected
items.fact: `H` hides selected items.
items.explanation: Hidden items are temporarily removed from the visible working view.

items.title: Hide Unselected
items.fact: `Shift`-`H` hides unselected items.
items.explanation: This isolates the current selection by hiding everything else.

items.title: Reveal Hidden
items.fact: `Alt`-`H` reveals hidden items.
items.explanation: Objects or mesh elements hidden with the relevant hide command become visible again.

items.title: Toolbar Toggle
items.fact: `T` toggles the Toolbar.
items.explanation: It shows or hides the left-side tool region in supported editors.

items.title: Sidebar Toggle
items.fact: `N` toggles the Sidebar.
items.explanation: The Sidebar exposes contextual properties in the editor.

items.title: Edit Mode
items.fact: `Tab` toggles Edit Mode in the 3D Viewport.
items.explanation: Edit Mode is used to directly edit mesh geometry.

items.title: Pose Mode
items.fact: `Ctrl`-`Tab` can toggle Pose Mode for armatures.
items.explanation: Pose Mode is used for posing armature bones.

items.title: Vertex Selection
items.fact: `1` selects vertex-selection mode in Edit Mode.
items.explanation: The mesh can be edited with vertices as the active selection element.

items.title: Edge Selection
items.fact: `2` selects edge-selection mode in Edit Mode.
items.explanation: Edges become the active mesh selection element.

items.title: Face Selection
items.fact: `3` selects face-selection mode in Edit Mode.
items.explanation: Faces become the active mesh selection element.

items.title: View Pie
items.fact: The backtick key opens the 3D Viewport navigation pie menu.
items.explanation: The pie menu provides quick access to view directions and related navigation options.

items.title: Gizmo Toggle
items.fact: `Ctrl`-backtick toggles gizmos in the 3D Viewport.
items.explanation: Gizmos are on-screen interactive controls for transformations and tools.

items.title: Fly or Walk
items.fact: `Shift`-backtick starts Fly/Walk Navigation.
items.explanation: This provides an alternative way to move through a 3D scene.

items.title: Insert Keyframe
items.fact: `I` inserts a keyframe.
items.explanation: A keyframe stores a value of an animatable property at the current frame.

items.title: Clear Keyframe
items.fact: `Alt`-`I` clears the keyframe.
items.explanation: It removes the keyframe from the current property context.

items.title: Clear All Keyframes
items.fact: `Shift`-`Alt`-`I` clears all keyframes.
items.explanation: This removes keyframes from the relevant animated data.

items.title: Add Driver
items.fact: `Ctrl`-`D` assigns a driver.
items.explanation: A driver lets one property be controlled by another value or expression.

items.title: Clear Driver
items.fact: `Ctrl`-`Alt`-`D` clears a driver.
items.explanation: The property stops being controlled by its driver.

items.title: Copy Python Operator
items.fact: `Ctrl`-`C` while hovering an operator button copies its Python command.
items.explanation: This is useful for learning or reusing the corresponding Python operation.

items.title: Copy Data Path
items.fact: `Shift`-`Ctrl`-`C` while hovering a field copies its relative data path.
items.explanation: The data path can be used in drivers or Python scripts.

items.title: Copy Full Data Path
items.fact: `Shift`-`Ctrl`-`Alt`-`C` copies a field’s full data path.
items.explanation: A full data path identifies the property from its data hierarchy.

items.title: Precise Drag
items.fact: Holding `Shift` while dragging makes value changes more gradual.
items.explanation: This is useful when finer control is needed during transformations or numeric dragging.

items.title: Coarse Snap
items.fact: Holding `Ctrl` while dragging snaps to coarse increments.
items.explanation: It can make exact rotations such as 90 degrees easier to achieve.

items.title: Fine Snap
items.fact: Holding `Shift`-`Ctrl` while dragging snaps to fine increments.
items.explanation: This combines slower adjustment with snapping for controlled values.

items.title: Shortcut Drills
items.fact: Practice `G`, `R`, and `S` conceptually through the Move, Rotate, and Scale tools, while confirming precise operations through Blender’s documented transform controls.
items.explanation: The manual documents these transformation tools and precision modifiers; a learner can turn them into short repetition drills.

items.title: Navigation Drill
items.fact: Practice orbit, pan, zoom, Frame All, and Frame Selected as a five-step viewport routine.
items.explanation: These are all documented navigation operations and together cover the basic actions needed to inspect a scene.

source.name: Blender Practice and Workflow Tips Derived from Official Manual

items.title: Local View Drill
items.fact: Select one or more objects, enter Local View, edit or inspect them, then return to Global View.
items.explanation: Local View is specifically documented for isolating selected objects and is useful practice for managing dense scenes.

source.name: Blender Practice and Workflow Tips Derived from Official Manual

items.title: Modifier Stack Drill
items.fact: Build a small test object and experiment with changing modifier order before applying any modifier.
items.explanation: Blender explicitly documents that stack order affects the result and that modifiers remain non-destructive until applied.

source.name: Blender Practice and Workflow Tips Derived from Official Manual

items.title: UV Distortion Drill
items.fact: Unwrap a simple mesh, add a test image, and inspect stretching before manually adjusting UVs.
items.explanation: This mirrors Blender’s documented general UV workflow.

source.name: Blender Practice and Workflow Tips Derived from Official Manual

items.title: Sculpt Scale Check
items.fact: Before sculpting, check whether the mesh scale has been applied.
items.explanation: Blender explicitly warns that applying scale helps make sculpt brush behavior predictable.

source.name: Blender Practice and Workflow Tips Derived from Official Manual

items.fact: Render the same simple scene in EEVEE and Cycles and compare the visual result.

items.title: Curve Geometry
items.fact: Blender curves are defined by mathematical functions rather than only straight interpolation between points.
items.explanation: Curves provide smooth procedural paths using control points.

items.title: Bezier Curve
items.fact: Blender supports Bézier curves.
items.explanation: Bézier curves are widely used for controllable smooth shapes.

items.title: NURBS Curve
items.fact: Blender supports NURBS curves.
items.explanation: NURBS curves use control points and mathematical interpolation.

items.title: Bézier Control Points
items.fact: Bézier curves generally start and end at their control points.
items.explanation: This makes their editing behavior intuitive for many modeling tasks.

items.title: NURBS Efficiency
items.fact: The Blender manual notes that NURBS can be more efficient to calculate when there are many twists and turns.
items.explanation: The mathematical representation can be advantageous for complex curved paths.

items.title: Curves Use Less Modeling Data
items.fact: Curves can represent shapes with less data than equivalent polygonal meshes at modeling time.
items.explanation: The procedural representation can reduce memory and storage requirements during modeling.

items.title: Curve Render Cost
items.fact: The procedural nature of curves can increase demands at render time.
items.explanation: A compact modeling representation does not automatically mean lower rendering cost.

items.title: Curve Profile Along Path
items.fact: Some modeling techniques are possible only with curves, such as extruding a profile along a path.
items.explanation: A profile can follow a curve to create elongated or swept forms.

items.title: Curve Vertex Control
items.fact: Fine vertex-level control is harder with curves than with meshes.
items.explanation: When exact individual-vertex editing is needed, mesh editing can be more suitable.

items.title: Bézier for Logos
items.fact: Bézier curves are commonly used for letters and logos.
items.explanation: Smooth controllable outlines are well suited to graphic forms.

items.title: Curve Motion Path
items.fact: Curves can be used as paths for animated objects.
items.explanation: An object can follow a curve-based path over time.

items.title: F-Curves
items.fact: Curves also represent animated properties as functions of time.
items.explanation: An F-Curve defines how an animation value changes between keyframes.

items.title: Merge by Distance Node
items.fact: Merge by Distance merges selected mesh vertices or point-cloud points that are within a chosen distance.
items.explanation: It can remove nearby duplicate points and merge their surrounding geometry.

source.name: Blender Geometry Nodes Merge by Distance

items.title: Selection Input
items.fact: Merge by Distance has a Selection input controlling which points participate.
items.explanation: Unselected points do not get merged into other points and are not merge targets.

source.name: Blender Geometry Nodes Merge by Distance

items.title: Selection for Performance
items.fact: Blender notes that selecting only needed points can improve performance because proximity searching is relatively expensive.
items.explanation: Reducing the number of candidates can reduce the search work.

items.title: All Merge Mode
items.fact: All mode can merge all relevant geometry, including loose parts.
items.explanation: Disconnected geometry can therefore participate in the distance-based merge.

source.name: Blender Geometry Nodes Merge by Distance

items.title: Connected Merge Mode
items.fact: Connected mode limits merging to attached geometry.
items.explanation: Loose disconnected parts are not merged together in this mode.

source.name: Blender Geometry Nodes Merge by Distance

items.title: Distance Threshold
items.fact: The Distance input controls how close points must be to be merged.
items.explanation: A larger threshold considers more nearby points as merge candidates.

items.fact: The node is similar to the Merge operator and Weld Modifier.
items.explanation: These tools address related workflows for combining nearby geometry.

items.title: Geometry Nodes
items.fact: Geometry Nodes is Blender’s node-based system for modifying object geometry.
items.explanation: Nodes perform operations that can create, alter, organize, and output geometry.

items.title: Geometry Nodes Modifier
items.fact: Geometry Nodes is accessed by adding a Geometry Nodes Modifier and setting up nodes in the Geometry Node Editor.
items.explanation: The modifier provides the connection between the object and the node tree.

items.title: Node Group
items.fact: The geometry-node tree connected to a modifier is a Node Group.
items.explanation: The group contains the procedural geometry logic.

items.title: Group Input
items.fact: Geometry entering the Geometry Nodes modifier is passed into the Group Input node.
items.explanation: The input provides the starting geometry or parameters for the node network.

items.title: Group Output
items.fact: Geometry Nodes pass the processed geometry to the Group Output node.
items.explanation: The output becomes the evaluated geometry for the next stage of the modifier stack.

items.title: Mesh Geometry Nodes
items.fact: Geometry Nodes can modify meshes.
items.explanation: Mesh data can be procedurally generated or transformed.

items.title: Curve Geometry Nodes
items.fact: Geometry Nodes can modify curves.
items.explanation: Curve data can participate in node-based procedural workflows.

items.title: Point Cloud Geometry Nodes
items.fact: Geometry Nodes can modify point clouds.
items.explanation: Point data can be procedurally processed.

items.title: Volume Geometry Nodes
items.fact: Geometry Nodes can modify volumes.
items.explanation: Volumes can be processed inside procedural node networks.

items.title: Instance Geometry Nodes
items.fact: Geometry Nodes can modify instances.
items.explanation: Instancing supports efficient repetition of reusable geometry.

items.title: Geometry Nodes on Empties
items.fact: Geometry Nodes can modify supported Empty objects.
items.explanation: An Empty can serve as an object context for a Geometry Nodes setup where supported.

items.title: Field Definition
items.fact: A field is fundamentally a function that transforms inputs into an output.
items.explanation: The same field definition can be evaluated repeatedly for different geometry elements.

items.title: Field Evaluation per Element
items.fact: Fields can calculate results independently for many elements such as mesh vertices or faces.
items.explanation: This is a core reason Geometry Nodes can create element-wise procedural effects.

items.title: Set Position Example
items.fact: A field connected to Set Position can depend on Position and Index and produce a vector transformation.
items.explanation: This demonstrates how multiple inputs can generate a per-element position change.

items.title: Field Socket Visualization
items.fact: Field connections are drawn as dashed lines in the node editor.
items.explanation: The line style indicates a field-based connection.

items.title: Field Type Error
items.fact: Connecting a non-field socket to a field socket produces a solid red error connection.
items.explanation: The visual error indicates an incompatible node connection.

items.title: Modeling Tools in Blender
items.fact: Blender provides modeling tools for meshes, curves, metaballs, and text objects.
items.explanation: Mesh modeling is the most common approach for creating 3D characters and environments, working with vertices, edges, and faces. Curves create smooth paths and organic shapes. Metaballs produce organic, blob-like forms that merge together. Text objects allow for 3D typography.

items.explanation: The command builds new geometry from the current vertex selection.

items.fact: With two vertices selected, `F` creates an edge.

items.title: More Than Four Vertices
items.fact: Selecting more than four vertices and pressing `F` can create a single n-gon.

items.fact: A chain of selected edges can be used to create a face.

items.title: Mesh Primitive
items.fact: Blender provides primitive mesh shapes that can be used as modeling starting points.
items.explanation: Primitive geometry gives artists simple forms to edit into more complex models.

items.title: Plane Primitive
items.fact: Blender's Plane primitive is a planar mesh starting point.
items.explanation: A flat plane can be reshaped or extruded as part of modeling.

items.title: Planar Mesh to Volume
items.fact: A planar mesh can be made three-dimensional by moving one or more vertices out of its plane.
items.explanation: Simple flat primitives can therefore become volumetric forms through modeling operations.

items.title: Circle Primitive
items.fact: Blender's Circle primitive can be used as a starting point for complex meshes.
items.explanation: A simple circular topology can be extended and reshaped into more detailed forms.

items.title: Grid Primitive
items.fact: Blender's Grid primitive is a subdivided plane.
items.explanation: The grid gives an evenly subdivided surface useful for landscapes and organic surfaces.

items.title: Monkey Primitive
items.fact: Blender's Monkey adds a stylized monkey head used as a test mesh.
items.explanation: The object, named Suzanne, is commonly used to test modeling and subdivision features.

items.title: UV Sphere
items.fact: Blender provides a UV Sphere primitive.
items.explanation: It is a common spherical starting shape for modeling.

items.title: Icosphere
items.fact: Blender provides an Icosphere primitive made from triangular faces.
items.explanation: It offers an alternative spherical topology to the UV Sphere.

items.title: Icosphere Subdivision
items.fact: Increasing an Icosphere subdivision splits each triangular face into four triangles.
items.explanation: More subdivisions increase the geometric resolution.

items.title: Cylinder Primitive
items.fact: Blender provides a Cylinder primitive.
items.explanation: The cylinder is a useful base shape for many manufactured and organic forms.

items.title: Cone Primitive
items.fact: Blender provides a Cone primitive.
items.explanation: A cone supplies a tapered starting shape for modeling.

items.title: Primitive UV Generation
items.fact: Blender primitives can generate UVs when the option is enabled.
items.explanation: UV coordinates allow textures to be mapped to the generated geometry.

items.title: Select Tool
items.fact: The Select tool selects or moves mesh components.
items.explanation: Selection determines which geometry subsequent editing operations affect.

items.title: Box Select
items.fact: Box Select chooses geometry by dragging a rectangle.
items.explanation: It is useful for selecting a region of mesh elements quickly.

items.title: Circle Select
items.fact: Circle Select chooses geometry inside a circular selection region.
items.explanation: The circular area makes broad local selections convenient.

items.title: Lasso Select
items.fact: Lasso Select chooses geometry inside a hand-drawn lasso.
items.explanation: It allows irregular selection shapes.

items.title: 3D Cursor Tool
items.fact: The Cursor tool changes the location of the 3D Cursor.
items.explanation: The 3D Cursor is a scene reference point used by placement and transformation tools.

items.title: Move Tool
items.fact: The Move tool performs translation.
items.explanation: Translation changes an element or object’s position.

items.title: Rotate Tool
items.fact: The Rotate tool rotates selected elements.
items.explanation: Rotation changes orientation around a pivot.

items.title: Scale Tool
items.fact: The Scale tool changes size.
items.explanation: Scaling enlarges or reduces selected geometry along chosen axes.

items.title: Scale Cage
items.fact: Scale Cage changes scale using a cage representation.
items.explanation: The cage gives a visual representation for the scaling operation.

items.title: Transform Tool
items.fact: The Transform tool combines translation, rotation, and scale manipulation.
items.explanation: It provides several common transformation controls in one tool.

items.title: Measure Tool
items.fact: The Measure tool measures distances in the scene.
items.explanation: It provides a visual distance check while working in the viewport.

items.title: Add Cube Tool
items.fact: The Add Cube tool interactively adds a cube mesh.
items.explanation: A cube is a common starting primitive for blockout and hard-surface modeling.

items.title: Add Cone Tool
items.fact: The Add Cone tool interactively adds a cone mesh.
items.explanation: The cone primitive provides an editable pointed base shape.

items.title: Add Cylinder Tool
items.fact: The Add Cylinder tool interactively adds a cylinder mesh.
items.explanation: The cylinder is useful as a starting form for many mechanical or organic parts.

items.title: Add UV Sphere Tool
items.fact: The Add UV Sphere tool interactively adds a UV sphere mesh.
items.explanation: A UV sphere provides a common rounded primitive for modeling.

items.title: Add Icosphere Tool
items.fact: The Add Icosphere tool interactively adds an icosphere mesh.
items.explanation: An icosphere provides a triangular sphere primitive.

items.title: Extrude Region
items.fact: Extrude Region extends a selected region together freely or along an axis.
items.explanation: Extrusion creates additional geometry connected to the selected region.

items.title: Extrude Manifold
items.fact: Extrude Manifold extrudes a region and dissolves overlapping geometry.
items.explanation: It is designed for extrusion workflows where overlapping geometry should be removed.

items.title: Extrude Along Normals
items.fact: Extrude Along Normals moves an extruded region along its normals.
items.explanation: The operation follows the surface direction of the selected region.

items.title: Extrude Individual
items.fact: Extrude Individual extrudes each selected element along its local normal.
